geeklist.title: MetaList for GeekList AUCTIONS
geeklist.description:
This MetaList is a current collection of Active GeekList Auctions. By posting your auction here, all subscribers will be notified of your sales.
BGG is a great avenue for finding the board games that you want. Most players take care of their games allowing for decent re-sale value. However, BGG in its current state is not an ideal place to host an auction. The community has developed a work around to make this feasible for as many people as possible. Because of the limitations, certain guidelines are needed. Please follow the rules below for all roles that are applicable to you.
[center][b][u]*** [size=15]I[/size][size=13]MPORTANT[/size] [size=15]I[/size][size=13]NSTRUCTIONS[/size] ***[/u][/b][/center]
[q][size=12][b]Instructions for Sellers:[/b][/size]
After you have created your GeekList Auction, please [b]post a single GeekList item[/b] linked directly to your auction GeekList. 1) Copy the URL of your GeekList Auction 2) At the bottom of this header, click on the white + in the blue box. 3) Paste the URL of your GeekList Auction 4) Click "Next →" 5) You may change or add an Image, by copying and pasting the Image Number (found within the URL of the image, e.g., https://boardgamegeek.com/image/[bgcolor=yellow]7596858[/bgcolor]/) 6) Click "Continue" 7) A new Item will appear on the GeekList. Please add the information listed below. 8) Confirm all information is correct [i]before [/i]clicking "✓ Save"
[size=11]Please include the following: [b]* End date[/b] (in bold or highlighted text) [b]* Any or all Items listed in the auction [/b](you may use the GeekList ImageID to highlight an item) [b]* Indicate in your own GeekList that BGG is to get their 3% commission and that your list is NOT set to private[/b] (other wise it will appear as not existing to us) [b]* Any other relevant information or special exceptions to your auction, such as... ** Shipping restrictions[/b] (US Only? Local Pick-up available?), [b]** Payment options [/b](Buy-it-Now prices? PayPal only?) [b]** Trades considered, etc.[/b]
[b][COLOR=#CC0000]Please modify the content of your GeekList Item [u]ONLY ONCE[/u] (preferably within 24 hours [i]remaining [/i]in your auction). This will notify all people that are subscribed to this MetaList.
For additional information, corrections, or reminders of end times, please only post as a [i]NEW COMMENT[/i] to your GeekList Item.
Be advised that if you break this rule, you will most likely receive GeekMail(s) reminding you of this guideline. Multiple infractions will result in your GeekList Item being deleted from the MetaList.
It is highly recommended that when you close your Auction, especially if it ends at a "random time", that you turn off Comments on your GeekList. Click on "Edit Descriptions & Header" in your Auction header. Uncheck "Allow Comments" under List Settings. This will prevent bids from coming in after the deadline. Once you record who is the high bid at the deadline, you can turn Comments back on if so desired.
Once the auction has been completed for a few days, please delete your GeekList Item on this MetaList so this MetaList can remain free of old content [i](do NOT edit it to mark it "CLOSED")[/i].[/COLOR][/b][/size]
Editing the title of YOUR GeekList to show it is closed is the best way to notify the community your Auction is closed. You should not delete your GeekList until all items have been received by bidders and any issues resolved.
If you plan on doing a follow-up auction of unsold items, you may either post a new entry (preferred) or modify the original (indicating it is a new auction in the posting). Periodically, the list will be scrubbed of auctions that have been closed for several days.
It is requested (but not required) that you link this MetaList in the comment section of your auction. This will help advertise this MetaList to the benefit of future sellers just as those that came before have helped you! This is GeekListID# 66420.
If any thing is unclear or you have a question, please contact me via GeekMail [b]prior[/b] to posting your Auction here.[/q]
[q][size=12][b]Instructions for Bidders:[/b][/size]
If you would like to be notified of new auctions, [i]please subscribe to [b]this MetaList[/b][/i].
* If you do not want to be notified of comments, you will need to modify the subscription by clicking the down arrow to the right of "Unsubscribe" in the header, then clicking on "Edit Subscription", then selecting "No" as a drop down under "Comment"; or try this link: https://boardgamegeek.com/subscription/edit/feed/geeklist/66420. ** [b]This is strongly recommended if you do not want the "noise" generated by user comments.[/b]
[COLOR=#CC0000]* Please also click the above link or "Edit Subscription" below to [b]ensure [/b]that [i]your[/i] personal default for "GeekList Item" does not resolve to "No" despite having subscribed. Otherwise you may not be notified of new auctions.[/COLOR]
* If you would like to be notified of new information of a specific auction, [i]please [u]also[/u] subscribe to [b]that specific GeekList Item[/b].[/i] This will override the general subscription setting of the MetaList. Any comment to that item will notify of the new content.
[b]* For discussion relevant to the general auction process, please comment on [thread=1901640][/thread]. For discussion relevant to a specific auction, please comment under that specific GeekList Item or within that Auction itself.[/b][/q]
[q][size=12][b]Miscellaneous Instructions:[/b][/size]
* Please only add a GeekList Item if it is [i]your[/i] auction. Sellers should have control of their own info. Instead, invite them to this thread to advertise.
* The rules included here are meant as a guideline for posting to this MetaList. For further guidelines on creating auctions, please see the wiki: https://www.boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/GeekList_auction
* Feel free to comment under any items but realize that each comment [b]will trigger all those subscribed to that item[/b]. Please keep it on point. It would be better to post any questions to the auction itself so anyone monitoring just that auction sees the discussion.
* If you want to comment on something posted under an auction that is not relevant to most subscribers (including rule infractions or discussing the infraction), [b]consider sending a polite and private GeekMail instead in order to avoid triggering a subscription notification[/b].
* As manager of this list, I reserve the right to make adjustments to the MetaList when deemed necessary. By posting on this MetaList, you are accepting these terms & conditions. [/q]

item.body:
[size=14]Public Service Announcement:[/size]
It is necessary to amend the rules of the MetaList for GeekList AUCTIONS. Due to the ongoing subscription notifications, I am reluctant to make modifications. Instead, I am going to maintain the official rules on this thread ([thread=1901640][/thread]) and link the following posts in the header. The main header will probably have some tl;dr rules with instruction to go to the thread for the full rules.
In addition, this will now also be the home for any and all discussion in regards to the MetaList. If there are any questions about the MetaList in general, application of rules, reporting of rules violations, suggested updates, it should be posted in the thread. Any comments for specific auctions can be directed under those entries, though I hope those remain at a minimum.
The first several posts are the current rules broken down by category. Updates will be a work in progress over the next few weeks. Once I feel they are ready enough to go live, I'll make a final edit to the header above, link to the thread and clean up the header. In the meantime, feel free to make any rule modification suggestions in the thread.
Probably the most needed update is the Auction Aggregator link and what, if anything, should replace it.
I'll let this entry cycle through the MetaList and remove it sometime after it has made its way to the top.

item.body:
I am running a monthly charity auction.
Every month I am listing at least one game.
The money raised by the auction, will every month be donated to a different help organization.
Aim of the geeklist is to put different help organizations into spotlight and encourage fellow geeks to donate for the good cause.
Running time: [b]Auctions start on the [b]first of the particular month[/b] and ends on [b]the last of the same month.[/b][/b]
Every listed game comes with [b]free worldwide shipping.[/b]
There is [b]no reserve[/b] on the items.
Won items can be paid by bank transfer, paypal or amazon.de gift voucher.
The complete amount raised by the auctions will go to the help organizations. Shipping costs and BGG fees are on me.
Geeklist Items so far:
- June 2014 [thing=107529][/thing] - July 2014 [thing=115][/thing] - August 2014 [thing=37907][/thing] to raise money for Ingenieure ohne Grenzen
[size=18]Please spread the word and join in bidding.[/size]

[center] [size=18]🌳 [b]Trees planted: 1772[/b] 🌳 🎋 [b]Projects supported: 12[/b] 🎋[/size][/center][hr]Hi. I'm Alex.
I'm splitting every buck I make from board games with our world by donating 50% of all [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/market/user/ZombieBoard][b]sales[/b][/url] and [url=https://ko-fi.com/zombieboard][b]donations[/b][/url] to a tree-planting charity. This geeklist is another way to generate more tree money and raise awareness of our planet's basic needs. Why 50% and not 100%? The remaining 50% will be used to acquire more games. More games mean more auctions, more trees planted, and more awareness in a hopeful, ever-bigger snowball of future saplings.
Here are the [b]rules of the game[/b]:
🌱 One game, or bundle, for auction around the start of the month until the last day (GMT time zone). 🌱 In the item's description, I'll spotlight the location in the world, which will receive 50% of the money raised to plant trees, through tree planting organizations. 🌱 I'll set up a Geekmarket sale for BGG's 3%. 🌱 [b][u]Free shipping worldwide is on me[/u][/b].
